title: The Midjourney formula for brand-consistent images
caption: Why your Midjourney images look random — and the 6-part prompt skeleton that makes them look like one brand. Save this.

slides.headline: The Midjourney formula for
slides.sub: Stop generating randomness. Build a house style.

slides.title: The 6-part skeleton
slides.body: Every prompt: [subject] + [composition] + [lighting] + [palette] + [medium/camera] + [negative]. Random prompts = random results. Same skeleton = a recognizable look.

slides.title: Lock the style reference
slides.body: Generate one image you love. Use it as --sref on every future prompt. This is the single biggest lever for 'all our images look related'.

slides.title: Fix the palette in words
slides.body: Don't say 'nice colors'. Say 'cream paper #F5F0E5, charcoal ink, one saturated red accent'. Specific hex-level language survives across generations.

slides.title: Commit to one lighting
slides.body: Pick one: 'soft north-window light' OR 'hard low rim light'. Mixing lighting across a feed is what makes a brand look amateur. Consistency reads as intentional.

slides.title: Write a house-style doc
slides.body: One paragraph that ends every prompt: the style, palette, lighting, and a negative list ('no 3D, no neon, no stock-photo gloss'). Paste it every time.

slides.title: Seed-lock for series
slides.body: Need 5 variations of the same scene? Reuse --seed. Changes stay controlled instead of regenerating a different universe each time.

slides.sub: The skeleton + a house-style template. Free.
